::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 30th [1873]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell
:::

My dear [Gertrude](people/person_751.qmd)
I hope your chapter[^1] will be of a length that will fit happily into July.  I will do my best for its coming in.  Here is your [Twilight](other_books/otherbook_834.qmd)[^2] which please look over, and it will get in when there is room. I do not think I am likely to come to London  I have had two outings - to Chichester in Easter week and last week to the laying the 1st stone of [Keble Chapel](organizations/other_5.qmd) and I don't think I shall make much of an expedition till the opening of [Mr Wither](people/person_1544.qmd)'s Church   I wish Crawley was on this side Winchester[^3]

yours very sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The first chapter of  G.L.J., 'The English Raja: James Brooke', was published in *MP* 16 (August 1873) 135-46, which ran until August 1874, and was published as Gertrude L. Jacob,  *The Raja of Saráwak : An account of Sir James Brooke, K.C.B., LL.D., given chiefly through letters and journals* (London: Macmillan 1876).
[^2]: G. L. J., 'Twilight' *MP* ns 16 (July 1873) 100-104.
[^3]: Jacob's father was Rector of Crawley, near Winchester.
